component.name: Apache NiFi
component.description: Framework for building processing pipelines using standard and custom components. The published security page combines a vulnerability reporting policy, a short security model delineating framework versus user responsibilities, CVSS-based severity ratings (critical: arbitrary remote code execution; high: integrity/availability compromise through resource exhaustion; medium: requires special configuration with significant mitigations available; low: minimal impact, difficult exploitation), and the archive of published vulnerabilities.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

threats.name: Code execution through operator-configured commands and custom code
threats.description: Components such as ExecuteProcess and ExecuteStreamCommand allow operating system command and custom code execution as a feature. Authenticated and authorized users bear responsibility for the security of the operating system commands and custom code they configure; configuring dangerous OS commands or untrusted custom scripts is not considered a project vulnerability subject to remediation.

threats.name: Exposure of the process management HTTP interface beyond localhost
threats.description: Framework process management uses the HTTP protocol and binds to localhost by default. Administrators who change the bind address assume responsibility for implementing additional protection strategies for the exposed interface.

controls.name: Design pipelines for the trust level of their input sources
controls.description: Privileged users must design processing pipelines with appropriate security measures based on the trust level of the input sources.

controls.name: Process management bound to localhost by default
controls.description: The framework's HTTP-based process management binds to localhost by default; administrators changing the bind address must add their own protection strategies.
